entries.summary: Vitamin B6 has limited, context-specific human evidence for PMS symptoms and a short high-dose anxiety signal, with important trial-quality and comparator limitations. Excess supplemental exposure can cause peripheral neuropathy; dose and duration matter.
entries.description: Vitamin B6 evidence is mixed and context-specific rather than high-confidence: PMS signals coexist with substantial risk-of-bias and comparator limitations, while high supplemental exposure carries a source-backed peripheral-neuropathy risk.
entries.safetyNotes: Avoid high or prolonged supplemental exposure without appropriate clinical context; peripheral neuropathy is the key dose- and duration-related safety limiter.

entries.summary: Phenylpropanoid found in aromatic plants that IARC classifies as probably carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A).
entries.description: Methyl eugenol is a naturally occurring flavour and fragrance compound. IARC classifies it as probably carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A) from sufficient experimental-animal and strong mechanistic evidence, while evidence regarding cancer in humans remains inadequate. That hazard classification does not quantify risk for every dose, route, or exposure matrix.
entries.safetyNotes: IARC classifies methyleugenol as probably carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A). Direct human cancer evidence is inadequate, and the classification does not provide one risk estimate for every exposure. Natural background, food, consumer-product, essential-oil, and concentrated isolated exposures are not interchangeable; avoid presenting concentrated methyleugenol as a wellness ingredient.
